Under the revisions, covered reporting markets, futures commission merchants, clearing members and foreign brokers report these contracts under parts 15 through 18 rather than certain sections of parts 38, 39, 43 and 45. entry.title: Cyber resilience: building confidence as threats evolve

entry.title: State Council Meeting Discusses Promoting Steady, Healthy Capital Market Development and Reviews Draft Regulation on Production Safety Accident Hazard Inspection

entry.title: SFC obtains disqualification orders against three former China Longevity directors

entry.title: Correction to data used in motor finance compensation calculation
entry.summary: Motor finance compensation scheme calculation FCA · Nov 26, 2026 · GuidanceThe FCA says it found errors in how it categorised a small group of loan agreements while preparing its response to legal challenges to its motor finance redress scheme. entry.title: How should investors evaluate fund performance?
entry.summary: How should investors evaluate performance? FCA · Nov 25, 2026 · GuidanceThe UK Financial Conduct Authority advises investors not to judge a fund only by whether its headline return beats a benchmark. Instead, investors should check the fund's stated objective, strategy and style, and whether it still fits their wider portfolio. The document notes that when a few large companies dominate markets, a more diversified fund may lag a concentrated index without the manager having made poor decisions. It also says style biases should be clearly disclosed and that managers must assess fund value annually.

entry.title: HKMA announces official launch of CMU Digital Asset Platform
entry.summary: Launch of CMU Digital Asset Platform HKMA · Nov 25, 2026 · Guidance · CryptoTopic evidence: 「Adopting an atomic Delivery versus Payment (DvP) on-chain settlement model, CMU DAP has direct interfaces with the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) systems and central bank digital currencies (CBDC)」 The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the official launch of the CMU Digital Asset Platform (CMU DAP), developed and operated by CMU OmniClear on its behalf. entry.title: CFTC Staff Advisory on Using Crypto Assets to Meet Financial Resources Requirements
entry.summary: CFTC Staff Issues Advisory Concerning the Use of Crypto Assets to Satisfy Financial Resources Requirements CFTC · Nov 23, 2026 · Guidance · CryptoTopic evidence: 「certain crypto assets, including bitcoin, ether, and payment stablecoins, may be counted toward the requirement to hold financial resources covering at least 12 months of operating costs」 The CFTC's Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk issued a staff advisory on how swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations may use crypto assets to meet their financial resources requirements. It says bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins may count toward holding resources that cover at least 12 months of operating costs, subject to appropriate haircuts. Because crypto assets are not "cash" or "highly liquid securities" under GAAP, they are not eligible for the separate liquidity requirement. The advisory reflects staff views only and does not create new rules or enforceable rights.

entry.title: Bereaved families need support rather than a struggle with paperwork
entry.summary: Bereaved families need support, not a battle with paperwork FCA · Nov 23, 2026 · ReportThe FCA reviewed how financial advisers, wealth managers and investment platforms support bereaved families and those handling estates. It found confusing communications, delays and gaps in support, and some firms still charged advice fees until an original death certificate was provided. The FCA says firms should explain next steps in plain English, offer several ways to report a death, keep paperwork proportionate and stop ongoing advice fees where the service is no longer provided.

entry.title: CFTC Charges 11 Companies and Two Indiana Executives in $550 Million Fraud Scheme
entry.summary: CFTC Charges 11 Companies and Two Indiana Executives in $550 Million Fraud Scheme CFTC · Nov 20, 2026 · EnforcementThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed a complaint in federal court in Indiana against two executives and 11 affiliated companies. It alleges they ran a Ponzi scheme that took more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants, claiming the money would fund leveraged forex trading. The complaint says little to no trading occurred, with funds misappropriated or used to pay fake profits, and solicitations continued through October 2026. The court froze assets and appointed a temporary receiver, and the CFTC seeks restitution, penalties, and a permanent injunction.
